A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BRICKGPT work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated limitations and assembly demonstrations.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on 250 prompts, quantitative baseline comparisons and ablations in Table 1, and manual and robotic assembly demonstrations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and demonstrations and adds quantitative results for stability-assisted baseline variants.

M1.justification: BRICKGPT retains the same LLaMA fine-tuning, brick representation, rejection sampling, physics-aware rollback and texturing/coloring procedures. Algorithm 1 is unchanged; the added stability-assisted procedures concern comparison baselines.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ShapeNetCore-derived StableText2Brick coverage of 21 categories and retain text-to-brick generation, texturing/coloring and physical assembly demonstrations. Additional layout sampling introduces no new dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds stability-assisted variants of all four mesh-based baselines: LLaMA-Mesh, LGM, XCube and Hunyuan3D-2. Retaining the original comparators while adding versions with stability-based selection substantially strengthens the central comparison.

E3.justification: The added baseline variants use multiple layouts per output mesh and accept the first stable layout: 10 attempts for LLaMA-Mesh/LGM and 100 for XCube/Hunyuan3D. This extends the evaluation protocol; the existing 250-prompt evaluation, held-out fraction, token cutoff and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds paired comparisons of mesh baselines with and without stability-assisted layout selection, testing the benefit of that augmentation. The BRICKGPT component ablations and Appendix A's nearest-neighbor novelty analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added 10/100 layout attempts serve candidate selection, not repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All original Table 1 numerical rows remain unchanged. Added stability-assisted variants report stability of 58.0% for LLaMA-Mesh, 32.5% for LGM, 83.6% for XCube and 88.4% for Hunyuan3D-2; BRICKGPT remains at 98.8%. Figure 5 also drops the square-seated-chair baseline comparison row, although BRICKGPT's example remains in Figure 6.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same mathematical content, including static-equilibrium constraints, the optimization objective and per-brick stability definition. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about stable text-to-brick generation, StableText2Brick, texturing and physical buildability. The additional baseline evidence supports existing claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of delayed stability checking, rejection sampling, rollback and low memorization retain their meaning. The limitations concerning grid resolution, category coverage and the fixed brick library move from Section 6 to Appendix D without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 documents generation budgets and the first-stable stopping criterion for the added baseline variants. Appendix A's training and inference details and the code/data/model access statements remain unchanged; the eight-brick inventory is relocated from the main text.

R1.justification: All 93 referenced works are retained. Section 2 removes the explicit characterization of Lennon et al. [31] as the closest goal and shortens its description from a text-image-voxel pipeline to image-to-voxel brick conversion. Existing reference [15] is additionally cited in the physics-simulation discussion.

P1.justification: v3 tightens wording across several sections and renames 'Mesh-to-Brick' to 'Shape-to-Brick.' Section 6 becomes 'Conclusion,' with limitations moved to Appendix D. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a separate stability-assisted baseline block and an explanatory caption. Figure 5 contracts from six comparison rows to five. The robotic assembly figure moves from main-text Figure 8 to appendix Figure 10, with other figures renumbered and the layout reflowed.

improvement.justification: v3 better tests the central stability advantage by adding stability-assisted mesh baselines and documenting their search budgets. The added Hunyuan3D-2 variant reaches 88.4% stability, while BRICKGPT's retained result is 98.8%, providing a stronger comparison. The budgets differ, so this is not a matched-compute test. These targeted evaluation gains outweigh the small loss of one qualitative comparison row; the method, coverage and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
